chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Asim ibn Humayd, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) did not cut the thief during the days of famine.

key_terms.يَقْطَعُ: He cuts (referring to amputation of the hand)

ai.seo_question: Did Amir al-Mu'minin cut the hand of thieves during famine?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of 'al-maslahah al-mursalah' (public interest) and the flexibility of hudud punishments in Shia jurisprudence, where the primary objective of justice is preserved by considering the thief's state of need. It reflects the practical application of Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) governance, prioritizing social welfare over rigid penal enforcement during periods of economic hardship. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that the conditions for qat' al-yad are not merely procedural but also substantive, requiring the absence of compelling need (hajah).

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from the one who informed him, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> did not cut the thief during the days of famine’.
